paper_type_evidence.quote: Using JWST/NIRSpec integral field spectroscopy, we derive the optical line ratios from the ISM and the CGM for our sample focusing on the typical optical lines used for metallicity studies.

results_numeric.quantity: SERRA galaxies with lower [CII]/Halpha in CGM

evidence.quote: we find that $19$ out of $20$ SERRA galaxies have lower $F_{\rm [\textup{C\,\textsc{\lowercase{ii}}}]}/F_{\rm H\alpha}$ ratios in the CGM than in the ISM

findings_qualitative.value: ISM and CGM have similar chemical abundances; oxygen ratio differences mainly from lower ionization in CGM; possible N/O deficit; elevated [CII]/Halpha in CGM

evidence.quote: Our comparison shows that the ISM and the CGM have similar chemical abundances.

claims.hypothesis: CGM is chemically enriched to ISM level at z~5
claims.experiment: Compare strong line ratios in ISM and CGM masks of 18 galaxies
claims.result: No significant difference in R23 and N2; marginal differences in O2, O32, O3, N2O2
claims.finding: CGM enriched to similar level as ISM

evidence.quote: This indicates that the CGM of these typical $4<z<6$ galaxies is enriched to the level of their ISM in the early universe.

claims.hypothesis: Oxygen line ratio differences arise from ionization
claims.result: Higher O2 and lower O32 reproduced by lower ionization

evidence.quote: a difference in ionization level (higher for the ISM) is the dominant reason for the observed ratio difference of oxygen line ratios.

claims.experiment: ALMA [CII] and JWST Halpha in masks; compare to SERRA
